Reservation of Seats for Scheduled Caste / Tribe (SC/ST) Candidates
• 22.5% of the numbers of seats in each of the non-JRF programmes are reserved for candidates
belonging to SC/ST (15% for SC and 7.5% for ST). However, reserved seats for ST candidates
remaining vacant after the ST Merit List is exhausted will be open to SC candidates and
vice-versa. If a seat of this category cannot be ﬁlled by eligible SC/ST candidates, it will
remain vacant.
• A candidate belonging to SC/ST category will get 30% relaxation on the General Qualifying
Score at each stage of the selection process.

• SC/ST students who get selected with respect to the general cut-off will not be considered as
part of this reserved quota. SC/ST candidates will be required to produce original Scheduled
caste/tribe certiﬁcate issued by a competent authority in the prescribed format at the time
of interview (if he/she is shortlisted for interview) or at the time of admission (if he/she is
offered admission without interview).
Reservation of Seats for Other Backward Classes - Non-Creamy layer (OBC-NCL)
• 27% seats of the numbers of seats in each of the non-JRF programmes are reserved for the
candidates belonging to OBC-NCL. Unﬁlled OBC-NCL seats will be dereserved.
• A candidate belonging to OBC-NCL category will get 10% relaxation on the General Quali-
fying Score at each stage of the selection process.

• A candidate belonging to OBC-NCL category will get 10% relaxation on the General Quali-
fying Score at each stage of the selection process.
• OBC-NCL candidates who get selected with respect to the general cut-off will not be con-
sidered as part of this reserved quota. OBC-NCL candidates will be required to produce
original certiﬁcate issued by a competent authority in the prescribed format at the time of
the interview (if he/she is shortlisted for interview) or at the time of admission (if he/she is
offered admission without interview).
Reservation of Seats for Economically Weaker Sections (GEN-EWS)
• Ten percent (10%) seats of the numbers of seats in each of the non-JRF programmes are
reserved for the candidates belonging to GEN-EWS. A candidate belonging to GEN-EWS
category will not get any relaxation on the General Qualifying Score at any stage of the
selection process.

• GEN-EWS seats will remain vacant in the absence of eligible candidates from the given

Reservation of Seats for Persons with Benchmark Disability (PwBD) Candidates
• Five percent (5%) of seats of the non-JRF programmes are horizontally reserved (that is, in
each of the categories ST, SC, OBC-NCL and GEN-EWS) for candidates with benchmark
disabilities, as per the Rights of Persons with Benchmark Disabilities Act, 2016, that is, the
beneﬁt of reservation will only be given to a candidate “with not less than forty per cent. of a
speciﬁed disability where speciﬁed disability has not been deﬁned in measurable terms and
includes a person with disability where speciﬁed disability has been deﬁned in measurable
terms, as certiﬁed by the certifying authority.”
• A candidate belonging to the PwBD category will get a relaxation of 30% on the General

terms, as certiﬁed by the certifying authority.”
• A candidate belonging to the PwBD category will get a relaxation of 30% on the General
Qualifying Score at each stage of the selection process. Such candidates will be required to
produce original certiﬁcate issued by district medical board/competent authority at the time
of the interview (if he/she is shortlisted for interview) or at the time of admission (if he/she
is offered admission without interview).

Candidates of OBC-NCL/ SC/ ST/ PwBD categories get relaxation on the General Qualifying
Score in their respective categories at each stage of the selection process.
For the JRF programmes in Statistics, Mathematics, Quantitative Economics and Computer Sci-
ence, the policy is the same as that for non-JRF programmes, described above.

Seats are not speciﬁcally reserved in the case of the other six JRF programmes. However, the
score of a candidate of the categories mentioned above will be multiplied by an appropriate factor
before the candidate is placed in the merit list. Such candidates will be required to produce original
certiﬁcate issued by a competent authority in the prescribed format at the time of the interview if
he/she is shortlisted for interview.
• The score of a candidate belonging to the SC/ST category will be multiplied by a factor of
10/7 before it is used for preparing the ﬁnal merit list.
• The score of a candidate belonging to the OBC-NCL category will be multiplied by a factor
of 10/9 before it is used for preparing the ﬁnal merit list.
• The score of a PwBD candidate, irrespective of the SC/ST/OBC-NCL/GEN-EWS/General
status, will be multiplied by a factor of 10/7 before it is used for preparing the ﬁnal merit
list.
